query: What are the common advantage attributes of airlines whose overall rating is high?

per_column.name: crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Categorical crew quality gives a clean grouping axis for identifying advantage attributes of high-rated airlines. Values align well with source text ('outstanding', 'consistently good', 'nice and helpful').

per_column.name: crew_proactive_care
per_column.rationale: A distinct proactive-care flag adds a genuine axis beyond raw quality. Mostly grounded (crew coming round with drinks, preparing beds), though row 3 marked False despite 'outstanding service' is a borderline/arguable read.

per_column.name: cultural_service_ethos
per_column.rationale: Service-culture style is a useful differentiator for airline advantage attributes. However groundedness is weak: rows explicitly mentioning 'Singaporean culture' and clearly SQ flights were labelled 'generic_professional', and the Gulf/omotenashi/European categories risk inferring airline identity not stated in the row text.

per_column.name: food_beverage_quality
per_column.rationale: Categorical food quality is a strong advantage-attribute axis. Values match text ('high quality', 'excellent', 'tasty steak'). NULLs for silent rows are appropriate.

per_column.name: meal_variety
per_column.rationale: Adds a variety dimension somewhat distinct from quality. Row 1's '2 full meals plus snacks' reasonably supports 'multiple_options'; other rows default to 'good_variety' which is a slightly generous read but not contradicted; NULLs appropriate.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_assessment
per_column.rationale: Well grounded (row 3 'uncomfortable'->poor, row 4 'bliss'->excellent), but largely redundant with the existing 'Seat Comfort' original column, reducing added analytical leverage.

per_column.name: seat_product_type
per_column.rationale: Hardware type is a legitimate new axis. But values often rely on inference not present in text: 'standard_recline' and 'flatbed' are asserted where source only says 'comfortable' or 'lie down bed'; the flatbed inference in row 4 is reasonable, but many standard_recline assignments are unsupported confident specifics.

per_column.name: special_service_recovery
per_column.rationale: Near-constant (87% false) limiting grouping value, though it captures a distinct recovery concept. Grounded: sampled rows show no recovery events and are marked False correctly.

per_column.name: value_for_money_perception
per_column.rationale: Somewhat redundant with existing 'Value For Money' column and heavily skewed to 'high_value' (near-constant). Groundedness is weak because none of the sampled review texts explicitly discuss price/value, yet 'high_value' is confidently asserted.

judge.rationale: The added columns give several genuinely useful axes (crew quality, food quality/variety, service ethos, seat product) for characterising advantage attributes of high-rated airlines, going beyond the original numeric ratings. Weaknesses: a few columns are near-constant or redundant with original rating columns (value_for_money_perception, seat_comfort_assessment, special_service_recovery), lowering leverage. Groundedness is generally solid for crew and food columns but degrades for inferential columns: cultural_service_ethos mislabels clearly Singaporean/SQ rows as 'generic_professional' and risks inferring airline identity, seat_product_type asserts specific hardware not stated, and value_for_money is confidently produced despite silent text. NULLs on silent rows are handled correctly and not penalised.
